title: A run stopped at its ceiling counts toward the loop's failure stop
body:
## Summary
runLoop counts a ceiling-stopped run as one of maxFailures, so three runs that hit their cost ceiling end the loop as failure-stopped, reported as "3 topics ended failed".

## Description
lib/articles/loop.ts:15-21 lists failure-stopped as "maxFailures topics ended failed (each already resumed maxResumes times)" and ceiling-stopped as per run, "marked for a human and never resumed". The worker's ceiling branch (lib/articles/loop.ts `one`, the `ceiling !== undefined` branch) does `failures++`, and a halted run does too. So a ceiling run, never resumed, is counted where the header says only runs resumed maxResumes times are, and the loop's stop reason names failures that were ceilings. Fixed means either the header says ceilings count toward the failure stop, or ceilings are tallied apart (their own stop, or none). Which one is the operator's call: it changes when a nightly --loop stops spending.

## Flow
- runLoop with maxFailures 1 and a ceiling under a run's price (articles-loop probe "a run over its cost ceiling") -> report.stop failure-stopped, report.runs[0].end ceiling-stopped
- the reason line says "1 topics ended failed" for a run that did not fail

## Expected impact
The operator reading loop.json learns the loop stopped on ceilings, not failures, or the loop keeps going past ceiling runs. Could break: a loop that today stops after three runaway runs would keep launching.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stop reason names what stopped the loop
Before: 1 of 1 ceiling-stopped runs counted as a failure; stop failure-stopped (articles-loop probe, cost ceiling case)
After: unmeasured - two designs, the choice is which number the operator wants a ceiling to move
Method: probe - the existing ceiling case reproduces the Before; the After depends on the decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: lib/articles/loop.ts:15-21 (header), lib/articles/lib/articles/loop.ts:474-475 `row.end = "ceiling-stopped"; failures++;`, tests/golden-path/articles-loop.probe.spec.ts "a run over its cost ceiling" expects stop failure-stopped

title: The loop's run ceilings and run estimate are literals beside the run price hint
body:
## Summary
DEFAULT_CEILINGS (120 USD / 30 USD / 45 turns) and DEFAULT_EST_RUN_USD (70) in lib/articles/loop.ts are written by hand next to a comment quoting the measured band that types.ts RUN_COST_HINT holds as data (47-92 USD, 26-32 turns).

## Description
fleet-orchestration/soft-budget-under-the-hard-cap: "the two numbers must be derived from one source" - a soft number and a hard cap written separately drift the first time either is tuned. types.ts:486 RUN_COST_HINT is the one spelling of a run's price (its own comment: "a second spelling of a price is how two surfaces come to disagree"), but loop.ts:232-236 restates its figures in prose and sets the ceilings and the estimate as independent literals. When RUN_COST_HINT moves (it says it will, when the model or roster changes), the loop's estimate and ceilings stay. Fixed: ceilings and estimate derived from RUN_COST_HINT (e.g. ceiling = usdHigh x margin, turns = turnsHigh + margin, estimate = midpoint), with the margins named.

## Flow
- RUN_COST_HINT.usdHigh is raised to 110 after a roster change
- DEFAULT_CEILINGS.runUsd stays 120: a normal run now sits within 10 USD of its ceiling
- the fix: derive the three numbers, pin the derivation in the loop probe

## Expected impact
Ceilings follow the measured price. It changes the numbers that stop paid runs (70 -> 69.5 for the estimate under a midpoint rule), so it is the operator's call.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for a run's price and the limits set from it
Before: 4 hand literals (120, 30, 45, 70) beside 4 data figures, 0 derived
After: 0 literals not derived, under margins the operator picks
Method: probe - counted on the tree; the After needs the margins
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: lib/articles/loop.ts:241-245 DEFAULT_CEILINGS / DEFAULT_EST_RUN_USD; lib/articles/types.ts:486 RUN_COST_HINT; ai-registry fleet-orchestration/techniques/soft-budget-under-the-hard-cap.md "The two numbers must be derived from one source"

title: The dry stand-in is found from process.cwd(), not from the engine's root
body:
## Summary
dryAgent.ts dryAgentBin resolves lib/articles/dryStandIn.mjs against process.cwd(), so a dry article job in a process whose cwd is not the repository root spawns a path that does not exist.

## Description
lib/articles/dryAgent.ts:35-38: with no ARTICLES_DRY_AGENT_BIN the argv is `[node, path.join(root, "lib", "articles", "dryStandIn.mjs")]` with `root = process.cwd()`. EngineDeps carries `root` (the repo root the prompt file is read from, lib/articles/engine.ts:51) but the dry turn (turns.ts standInTurn, called by the article job's dry port in packages/producers) never receives it. A worker or server started from another directory gets every dry turn back as "exited 1: Cannot find module" - a DRY run failing for a reason a live run would not have. Fixed: the stand-in path is resolved from the engine's root (passed through the turn) or from the module's own location.

## Flow
- start a process with cwd = workers/ and run a dry article job
- dryRunAgent spawns node workers/lib/articles/dryStandIn.mjs -> exit 1, no envelope
- the research step fails `the agent errored: exited 1: ... Cannot find module`

## Expected impact
Dry rehearsals behave the same from any working directory. Could break: a caller relying on cwd to pick a different stand-in (ARTICLES_DRY_AGENT_BIN is the documented override).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a dry turn's stand-in is found wherever the process started
Before: dryAgentBin({}, "C:/elsewhere") names C:/elsewhere/lib/articles/dryStandIn.mjs (read from the code; not spawned this round)
After: the stand-in under the repository root, whatever the cwd
Method: simulation - the seam that would carry `root` is in packages/producers (the dry port), outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/articles/dryAgent.ts:35-38 `root: string = process.cwd()`; lib/articles/dryAgent.ts:44 `const bin = dryAgentBin();` (no root passed); lib/articles/turns.ts standInTurn
instrument: a vitest case that calls standInTurn for a writer turn with process.chdir(os.tmpdir()) and asserts outcome completed (seed: today it returns errored with Cannot find module)

title: Two out-of-context follow-ups of this round: the CLI's damaged line, reviewerEngines' four
body:
## Summary
pipeline/article.mts prints a loop's orphaned runs but not the `damaged` list f24ea4a6 added, and lib/agent/reviewerEngines.ts:11 still says "four engines" over a three-engine roster.

## Description
f24ea4a6 made coverage() and the loop report carry `damaged` (run directories whose run.json does not parse); the CLI's loop summary (pipeline/article.mts:412) prints `orphaned` and would leave `damaged` in loop.json only. 91e653ec corrected the engine count in lib/articles/types.ts and engine.ts; lib/agent/reviewerEngines.ts's banner "Reviewers - four engines, one read-only profile" is the same claim (REVIEWER_ENGINES is claude | codex | agy since grok's descoping, 2026-10-14) and tests/golden-path/articles-critique.probe.spec.ts:3,90 repeat it. Both files are outside article-run-engine.

## Flow
- `npx tsx pipeline/article.mts loop ...` over a store with a broken run.json -> the summary names orphaned runs, not the damaged one
- add one line beside the orphaned one; correct the banner and the two probe comments

## Expected impact
The operator sees a damaged run in the terminal, not only in loop.json; the reviewer seam's header matches its roster. Could break: nothing - a print line and comments.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the CLI surfaces what the report carries; the seam's header states its roster
Before: 0 of 2 report lists printed for damaged; 3 "four engines" claims outside this context
After: 1 print line; 0 claims
Method: probe - grep on the tree (pipeline/article.mts:412, lib/agent/reviewerEngines.ts:11)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the loop CLI run against a sandbox store holding a broken run.json, asserting the stdout names it (seed: today it does not)
